sanskrit: pra mandine pitumad arcatā vaco yaḥ kṛṣṇagarbhā nirahann ṛjiśvanā | avasyavo vṛṣaṇaṁ vajradakṣiṇam marutvantaṁ sakhyāya havāmahe ||
english: Sing forth an invigorating, nourishing hymn of praise to him who drove out the black-bellied ones together with Ṛjiśvan; seeking his aid, we call upon the mighty one, right-handed with the thunderbolt, him accompanied by the Maruts, for friendship.

sanskrit: yo vyaṁsaṁ jāhṛṣāṇena manyunā yaḥ śambaraṁ yo ahan piprum avratam | indro yaḥ śuṣṇam aśuṣaṁ ny āvṛṇaṅ marutvantaṁ sakhyāya havāmahe ||
english: He who with exulting fury smote Vyaṁsa, who slew Śambara, who struck down lawless Pipru; Indra who turned back dry Śuṣṇa, who drains not — him, accompanied by the Maruts, we call for friendship.

sanskrit: yasya dyāvāpṛthivī pauṁsyam mahad yasya vrate varuṇo yasya sūryaḥ | yasyendrasya sindhavaḥ saścati vratam marutvantaṁ sakhyāya havāmahe ||
english: Whose virile might heaven and earth proclaim as great; in whose ordinance Varuṇa moves, in whose ordinance the sun; whose ordinance the rivers, Indra's rivers, follow — him, accompanied by the Maruts, we call for friendship.

sanskrit: yo aśvānāṁ yo gavāṁ gopatir vaśī ya āritaḥ karmaṇi-karmaṇi sthiraḥ | vīḻoś cid indro yo asunvato vadho marutvantaṁ sakhyāya havāmahe ||
english: Who is the sovereign lord of horses and of cattle, and who remains firm in every deed when invoked; Indra the strong, the death-blow to the one who presses no soma — him, accompanied by the Maruts, we call for friendship.

sanskrit: yo viśvasya jagataḥ prāṇatas patir yo brahmaṇe prathamo gā avindat | indro yo dasyūm̐r adharām̐ avātiran marutvantaṁ sakhyāya havāmahe ||
english: Who is the lord of all that breathes in the world, who first found the cows for the devotee; Indra who hurled the Dasyus downward — him, accompanied by the Maruts, we call for friendship.

sanskrit: yaḥ śūrebhir havyo yaś ca bhīrubhir yo dhāvadbhir hūyate yaś ca jigyubhiḥ | indraṁ yaṁ viśvā bhuvanābhi saṁdadhur marutvantaṁ sakhyāya havāmahe ||
english: He who is to be invoked by the brave and by the timid, who is called upon by those who race into battle and by those who have won; Indra, upon whom all the worlds have set their hopes — him, accompanied by the Maruts, we call for friendship.

sanskrit: rudrāṇām eti pradiśā vicakṣaṇo rudrebhir yoṣā tanute pṛthu jrayaḥ | indram manīṣā abhy arcati śrutam marutvantaṁ sakhyāya havāmahe ||
english: The all-seeing one goes in the quarters of the Rudras; the maiden stretches wide the expanse with the Rudras; with devotion one praises the renowned Indra — him, accompanied by the Maruts, we call for friendship.

sanskrit: yad vā marutvaḥ parame sadhasthe yad vāvame vṛjane mādayāse | ata ā yāhy adhvaraṁ no acchā tvāyā haviś cakṛmā satyarādhaḥ ||
english: Whether, O Indra attended by the Maruts, thou dost rejoice in the highest abode, or whether in the lower habitation — come hither to our sacrifice; for thy sake we have prepared the oblation, O true-gifted one.

sanskrit: tvāyendra somaṁ suṣumā sudakṣa tvāyā haviś cakṛmā brahmavāhaḥ | adhā niyutvaḥ sagaṇo marudbhir asmin yajñe barhiṣi mādayasva ||
english: For thee, O Indra of great skill, we have pressed the soma; for thy sake we have prepared the oblation, O thou who art borne by prayer; now with thy team of horses, together with the Maruts as thy company, rejoice at this sacrifice upon the sacred grass.

sanskrit: mādayasva haribhir ye ta indra vi ṣyasva śipre vi sṛjasva dhene | ā tvā suśipra harayo vahantūśan havyāni prati no juṣasva ||
english: Rejoice, O Indra, with thy bay horses; unloose thy cheeks, release the two reins; may thy bays bring thee, O thou of lovely chin, willing — accept our oblations with pleasure.

sanskrit: marutstotrasya vṛjanasya gopā vayam indreṇa sanuyāma vājam | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: May we, guarded by the praise of the Maruts, win the prize of strength together with Indra. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that boon.

sanskrit: imāṁ te dhiyam pra bhare maho mahīm asya stotre dhiṣaṇā yat ta ānaje | tam utsave ca prasave ca sāsahim indraṁ devāsaḥ śavasāmadann anu ||
english: I offer unto thee this great and mighty prayer — the intelligence attaches itself to the praise of this great one; him unconquered in contest and in battle, Indra, the gods exulted in his power one after another.

sanskrit: asya śravo nadyaḥ sapta bibhrati dyāvākṣāmā pṛthivī darśataṁ vapuḥ | asme sūryācandramasābhicakṣe śraddhe kam indra carato vitarturam ||
english: The seven rivers carry his glory; Heaven and Earth bear his fair form in their lap; in us the sun and moon, for their illumination, travel back and forth trustingly — grant us this, O Indra.

sanskrit: taṁ smā ratham maghavan prāva sātaye jaitraṁ yaṁ te anumadāma saṁgame | ājā na indra manasā puruṣṭuta tvāyadbhyo maghavañ charma yaccha naḥ ||
english: Urge forward that victorious chariot of thine, O Maghavan, to win the spoil — the chariot we have praised for thee in the encounter; drive it forward with thy mind, O Indra praised by many; grant shelter to those who are devoted to thee, O Maghavan.

sanskrit: vayaṁ jayema tvayā yujā vṛtam asmākam aṁśam ud avā bhare-bhare | asmabhyam indra varivaḥ sugaṁ kṛdhi pra śatrūṇām maghavan vṛṣṇyā ruja ||
english: May we conquer, with thee as our ally, the prize that is ours; lift up our share in battle after battle; make wide and easy room for us, O Indra; shatter the virile strength of our enemies, O Maghavan.

sanskrit: nānā hi tvā havamānā janā ime dhanānāṁ dhartar avasā vipanyavaḥ | asmākaṁ smā ratham ā tiṣṭha sātaye jaitraṁ hīndra nibhṛtam manas tava ||
english: For various clans call on thee, O upholder of wealth, with their praises, seeking thy aid; mount our chariot for the winning of the prize, for thy mind, O Indra, is set on victory.

sanskrit: gojitā bāhū amitakratuḥ simaḥ karman-karmaṁ chatamūtiḥ khajaṁkaraḥ | akalpa indraḥ pratimānam ojasāthā janā vi hvayante siṣāsavaḥ ||
english: His arms win cattle; boundless in counsel, unsurpassed, the hundredfold helper in every deed, the hero — Indra equalled none with his strength; and so the peoples who desire to conquer call upon him from every side.

sanskrit: ut te śatān maghavann uc ca bhūyasa ut sahasrād ririce kṛṣṭiṣu śravaḥ | amātraṁ tvā dhiṣaṇā titviṣe mahy adhā vṛtrāṇi jighnase puraṁdara ||
english: Thy glory among peoples rises above the hundred, above even more, surpasses a thousand; the intelligence intensifies thee, measureless and mighty; even so thou slayest the Vṛtras, O Puraṁdara, fort-destroyer.

sanskrit: triviṣṭidhātu pratimānam ojasas tisro bhūmīr nṛpate trīṇi rocanā | atīdaṁ viśvam bhuvanaṁ vavakṣithāśatrur indra januṣā sanād asi ||
english: The measure of thy might has a triple-threaded element; three are the earths, O lord of men, and three the bright realms; thou hast surpassed all this universe; without enemy from birth, thou art ever, O Indra.

sanskrit: tvāṁ deveṣu prathamaṁ havāmahe tvam babhūtha pṛtanāsu sāsahiḥ | semaṁ naḥ kārum upamanyum udbhidam indraḥ kṛṇotu prasave ratham puraḥ ||
english: Thee we invoke first among the gods; thou hast been the unconquered one in battles; may Indra drive this eager, most devoted, bursting-forth one's chariot of ours to the fore at the start of the contest.

sanskrit: tvaṁ jigetha na dhanā ruroddhithārbheṣv ājā maghavan mahatsu ca | tvām ugram avase saṁ śiśīmahy athā na indra havaneṣu codaya ||
english: Thou hast conquered; thou hast not shut off the spoils; in small battles and in great, O Maghavan — we sharpen thee, the fierce one, for our protection; now, O Indra, impel us forward in our invocations.

sanskrit: viśvāhendro adhivaktā no astv aparihvṛtāḥ sanuyāma vājam | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: May Indra be our advocate always; undeviated, may we win the prize. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that boon.

sanskrit: tat ta indriyas paramam parācair adhārayanta kavayaḥ puredam | kṣamedam anyad divy anyad asya sam ī pṛcyate samaneva ketuḥ ||
english: That highest power of thine, the seers of old established pointing outward; one part of it is here on earth, another in the sky — together they meet like a single standard of an army.

sanskrit: sa dhārayat pṛthivīm paprathac ca vajreṇa hatvā nir apaḥ sasarja | ahann ahim abhinad rauhinaṁ vy ahan vyaṁsam maghavā śacībhiḥ ||
english: He sustained the earth and spread it wide; having smitten with the thunderbolt, he released the waters; he slew the serpent, he cleft Rauhinī apart; Maghavan cut down Vyaṁsa with his mighty deeds.

sanskrit: sa jātūbharmā śraddadhāna ojaḥ puro vibhindan acarad vi dāsīḥ | vidvān vajrin dasave hetim asyāryaṁ saho vardhayā dyumnam indra ||
english: He, the strong-natured, placing faith in his might, went about shattering the fortresses, distributing among the Dāsīs; knowing, O Vajrin, hurl thy weapon at the Dasyu; increase the Aryan's dominion and glory, O Indra.

sanskrit: tad ūcuṣe mānuṣemā yugāni kīrtenyaṁ maghavā nāma bibhrat | upaprayann dasyuhatyāya vajrī yad dha sūnuḥ śravase nāma dadhe ||
english: That Maghavan, bearing a name worthy of praise, spoke to the ancient one for these ages of men; when the Vajrin advanced to slay the Dasyus and the son established a name for glory.

sanskrit: tad asyedam paśyatā bhūri puṣṭaṁ śrad indrasya dhattana vīryāya | sa gā avindat so avindat aśvān sa oṣadhīḥ so apaḥ sa vanāni ||
english: Behold this abundance, this great prosperity of his — place your faith in the heroic deeds of Indra; he found the cows, he found the horses, he found the herbs, he found the waters, he found the forests.

sanskrit: bhūrikarmaṇe vṛṣabhāya vṛṣṇe satyaśuṣmāya sunavāma somam | ya ādṛtyā paripanthīva śūro 'yajvano vibhajann eti vedaḥ ||
english: We press soma for the abundant-actioned bull, the vigorous one, whose strength is true; he who, like a hero lying in wait on the road, goes distributing spoil among those who do not sacrifice.

sanskrit: tad indra preva vīryaṁ cakartha yat santam vajreṇābodhayas ahim | anu tvā patnīr hṛṣitaṁ vayaś ca viśve devāso amadann anu tvā ||
english: Thou didst accomplish that heroic deed surpassing what had been done before, when thou didst rouse the lying serpent with the thunderbolt; the consorts and the birds rejoiced after thee, all the gods exulted after thee.

sanskrit: śuṣṇaṁ pipruṁ kuyavaṁ vṛtram indra yadāvadhīr vi puraḥ śambarasya | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Kuyava, and Vṛtra thou didst slay, O Indra, and didst shatter the fortresses of Śambara; may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that boon.

sanskrit: yoniṣ ṭa indra niṣade akāri tam ā ni ṣīda svāno nārvā | vimucyā vayo avasāyāśvān doṣā vastor vahīyasaḥ prapitve ||
english: A seat has been made for thee, O Indra, in which to sit; sit down therein like a mighty man, not like a steed; let loose the birds and unyoke the horses at the approach of evening and dawn, thou who art fit to carry us forward.

sanskrit: o tye nara indram ūtaye gur nū cit tān sadyo adhvano jagamyāt | devāso manyuṁ dāsasya ścamnan te na ā vakṣan suvitāya varṇam ||
english: Lo, those men have approached Indra for aid; may he reach them straightway even now on the path; the gods, having crushed down the wrath of the Dāsa, may they bring our tribe to well-being.

sanskrit: ava tmanā bharate ketavedā ava tmanā bharate phenam udan | kṣīreṇa snātaḥ kuyavasya yoṣe hate te syātām pravaṇe śiphāyāḥ ||
english: The all-knowing one draws by himself the wave downward, by himself draws down the foaming water; bathed in milk — may the two consorts of Kuyava, once he is slain, lie on the slope of the ravine.

sanskrit: yuyopa nābhir uparasya āyoḥ pra pūrvābhis tirate rāṣṭi śūraḥ | añjasī kuliśī vīrapatnī payo hinvānā udabhir bharante ||
english: The navel of the higher one's offspring has been severed; the hero surpasses with his ancient powers in ruling the land; the two gracious, axe-wielding wives of the hero, urging milk forward, bear it with the waters.

sanskrit: prati yat syā nīthādarśi daśyor oko nācchā sadanaṁ jānatī gāt | adha smā no maghavañ carkṛtād in mā no magheva niṣṣapī parā dāḥ ||
english: When that dwelling of the Dasyu was seen in the way, it did not go to the abode knowing its direction; therefore act for us, O Maghavan; do not abandon us as the generous man abandons the ungifted supplicant.

sanskrit: sa tvaṁ na indra sūrye so apsvānāgāstvā ā bhaja jīvaśaṁse | māntarāṁ bhujam ā rīriṣo naḥ śraddhitaṁ te mahata indriāya ||
english: Be thou for us, O Indra, blameless in the sun and in the waters; grant us a share in the praise of the living; do not cut short our portion in the middle; this we entrust in faith to thy great might.

sanskrit: adhā manye śrat te asmā adhāyi vṛṣā codasva mahate dhanāya | mā no akṛte puruhūta yonāv indra kṣudhyadbhyo vaya āsutim dāḥ ||
english: Now I believe faith has been placed in thee by us; O bull, urge us forward to great wealth; do not give our food-supply, O Indra much-invoked, to the hungry in an unworked condition.

sanskrit: mā no vadhīr indra mā parā dā mā naḥ priyā bhojanāni pra moṣīḥ | āṇḍā mā no maghavañ chakra nir bhen mā naḥ pātrā bhet sahajānuṣāṇi ||
english: Slay us not, O Indra, give us not away; steal not from us our dear enjoyments; shatter not our eggs, O Maghavan, O mighty one; break not the vessels that were born together with us.

sanskrit: arvāṅ ehi somakāmaṁ tvāhur ayaṁ sutas tasya pibā madāya | uruvyacā jaṭhara ā vṛṣasva piteva naḥ śṛṇuhi hūyamānaḥ ||
english: Come hither — they call thee the lover of soma; this soma is pressed, drink of it for exhilaration; fill thy wide belly as a bull; hear us as we call thee, as a father hears.

sanskrit: candramā apsvantara ā suparṇo dhāvate divi | na vo hiraṇyanemayaḥ padaṁ vindanti vidyuto vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: The moon runs in the waters, the eagle soars in the sky; the lightning-bolts with golden rims find not your track — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: artham id vā u arthinā ā jāyā yuvate patim | tuñjāte vṛṣṇyam payaḥ paridāya rasaṁ duhe vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: Only for a purpose does the wife draw her husband to her — the one who is in need; they press out the manly milk; having set aside the essence, they milk it — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: mo ṣu devā adaḥ svar ava pādi divas pari | mā somyasya śambhuvaḥ śūne bhūma kadā cana vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: May not, O gods, yonder sky fall down from heaven; may we never be in the void of the soma-yielding, the auspicious one — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: yajñam pṛcchāmy avamaṁ sa tad dūto vi vocati | kva ṛtam pūrvyaṁ gataṁ kas tad bibharti nūtano vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: I ask the lowest sacrifice; that messenger will proclaim it: where has the primordial order gone, who now carries it onward? — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: amī ye devāḥ sthana triṣv ā rocane divaḥ | kad va ṛtaṁ kad anṛtaṁ kva pratnā va āhutir vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: Ye gods who stand in the three bright regions of the sky — what is right and what is wrong among you? Where is your ancient oblation? — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: kad va ṛtasya dharṇasi kad varuṇasya cakṣaṇam | kad aryamṇo mahas pathāti krāmema dūḍhyo vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: What is the foundation of ṛta? What is the vision of Varuṇa? How shall we traverse the great path of Aryaman, we the perplexed? — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: ahaṁ so asmi yaḥ purā sute vadāmi kāni cit | tam māvyanty ādhyo vṛko na tṛṣṇajam mṛgaṁ vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: I am he who in an earlier time spoke certain things at the pressing of soma; afflictions assail me — like a wolf assailing a thirsty animal — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: sam mā tapanty abhitaḥ sapatnīr iva parśavaḥ | mūṣo na śiśnā vy adanti mādhyaḥ stotāraṁ te śatakrato vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: The ribs press against me on both sides like rival wives; the middle ones gnaw through like mice gnawing at sinews — they consume thy praiser, O Śatakratu of the hundred powers — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: amī ye sapta raśmayas tatra me nābhir ātatā | tritas tad vedāptyaḥ sa jāmitvāya rebhati vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: Those seven rays — my navel-cord is stretched out to them; Trita Āptya knows that and sings it to make kin — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: amī ye pañcokṣaṇo madhye tasthur maho divaḥ | devatrā nu pravācyaṁ sadhrīcīnā ni vāvṛtur vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: Those five bulls who stand in the midst of the great heaven — those that are worthy to be proclaimed among the gods have turned back all together — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: suparṇā eta āsate madhya ārodhane divaḥ | te sedhanti patho vṛkaṁ tarantaṁ yahvatīr apo vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: The eagles sit in the intermediate region of the ascent of the sky; they ward off from the paths the wolf who crosses over the swiftly flowing waters — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: navyaṁ tad ukthyaṁ hitaṁ devāsaḥ supravācanam | ṛtam arṣanti sindhavaḥ satyaṁ tātāna sūryo vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: That new recitable hymn, set forth for the gods, easy to proclaim: the rivers flow with ṛta, the sun has spread truth — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: agne tava tyad ukthyaṁ deveṣv asty āpyam | sa naḥ satto manuṣvad ā devān yakṣi viduṣṭaro vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: That recitable thing of thine, O Agni, belongs to the gods as their treasure; do thou, seated there more wisely than Manu, worship the gods for us — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: satto hotā manuṣvad ā devām̐ acchā viduṣṭaraḥ | agnir havyā suṣūdati devo deveṣu medhiro vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: The Hotṛ-priest seated there, wiser than Manu, faces the gods; Agni, the wise god among gods, well sets the oblations moving — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: brahmā kṛṇoti varuṇo gātuvidaṁ tam īmahe | vy ūrṇoti hṛdā matiṁ navyo jāyatām ṛtaṁ vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: Brahmā Varuṇa makes the path-knowing one; we implore him; he uncovers with the heart the thought — may the new ṛta be born — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: asau yaḥ panthā ādityo divi pravācyaṁ kṛtaḥ | na sa devā atikrame tam martāso na paśyatha vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: Yonder path of the sun set in the sky to be proclaimed — O gods, that one none transgresses; O mortals, ye do not see it — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: tritaḥ kūpe avahito devān havata ūtaye | tac śuśrāva bṛhaspatiḥ kṛṇvann aṁhūraṇād uru vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: Trita, cast down into the well, calls upon the gods for aid; Bṛhaspati heard this and made wide space from the narrow confine — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: aruṇo māṁ sakṛd vṛkaḥ pathā yantaṁ dadarśa hi | uj jihīte nicāyyā taṣṭeva pṛṣṭyāmayī vittam me asya rodasī ||
english: The tawny wolf once saw me as I was going along the path; the one who must be kept hidden rises up, sick in the spine like a carpenter's wife — understand this for me, O heaven and earth.

sanskrit: enāṅgūṣeṇa vayam indravanto abhi ṣyāma vṛjane sarvavīrāḥ | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: With this hymn of praise, attended by Indra, may we overcome in the settlement, full of all heroes; may Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us that boon.
